findings.description: CON-SUP-101 requires T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT to be released in that order each 10 ms cycle. SYS-CFG-002 gives their configured periods and SYS-CFG-004 gives checkpoint order. An implementation can release the three tasks in a different order and still produce checkpoints in the configured order.
findings.requested_change: Capture the required default release sequence separately from checkpoint order and trace it to CON-SUP-101.

findings.description: SYS-RST-012 requires a software reset for configuration-integrity failure while SYS-RST-003 latches the safe state for a range fault. SYS-MEM-002 and SYS-CFG-008 leave open whether a corrupted block can be range-checked and latch the safe state before its failed CRC comparison is known. CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-115 do not settle which outcome applies when both checks fail.
findings.requested_change: Record and resolve the validity and precedence rules for startup checks when an integrity failure and a range violation can both be observed. Apply the agreed diagnostic and recovery outcomes to that case.

findings.description: After a repeated-fault latch and a subsequent startup that passes all checks, SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011 hold the external signals low. The set leaves it open whether application releases, alive supervision and runtime integrity checking proceed in that state. SYS-MEM-004, SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-MEM-008 use startup-check completion without a common mode rule for retained-latch startup.
findings.requested_change: Disposition which application and supervisor functions are active when startup checks pass with the safe state still latched, and align their entry conditions with the agreed behavior under CON-SUP-110.

findings.description: The startup message, asynchronous fault reports and service replies use the same CON-SUP-007 serial line. SYS-RST-009, SYS-DIAG-002 and SYS-DIAG-007 through SYS-DIAG-009 do not say how an in-progress response or multiple pending reports are handled when a fault report becomes due. OP-SYS-033 covers a later fault near software reset, leaving transmission already in progress and simultaneous demand open.
findings.requested_change: Identify the permitted concurrent traffic and frame-handling rules. Check the admitted report and reply lengths and scheduling against the 115200 baud line and the applicable deadlines.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 gives a configuration block with a stored CRC, and SYS-CFG-001 and SYS-MEM-002 depend on the same block. OP-SYS-005 records CRC algorithm parameters but leaves the byte range and treatment of the stored CRC field unspecified. A producer and checker can use the same CRC parameters and disagree on the result.
findings.requested_change: Record the configuration producer/checker interface decision for the covered bytes, their serialization and the treatment of the stored CRC field. Use it to define reproducible valid and invalid blocks.

findings.description: Several rationales direct readers to the wrong requirement after the fault-reaction items were split. SYS-SAFE-007 and SYS-SAFE-008 point to SYS-SAFE-003 for the latched hold, which is now in SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011. SYS-RST-012 points to SYS-RST-002 for report-before-reset ordering, which is stated in SYS-RST-013.
findings.requested_change: Update the rationales and open-point references to identify the current requirements that own each hold, transition and ordering rule.

findings.description: STK-SUP-005 limits service of both watchdogs to healthy tasks. SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-WDG-007 treat a detectable task fault as the end of health for window-watchdog service. SYS-WDG-004 and SYS-WDG-005 still use declaration for independent-watchdog service, so a pending declaration can leave an independent refresh required after the set already treats the task as unhealthy.
findings.requested_change: Define the health transition that governs each watchdog. Use the same transition unless an approved distinction explains how both service rules satisfy STK-SUP-005.

findings.description: SYS-RST-002 defines an entry instant per fault, including when all three signals are already low at detection. SYS-RST-001 starts the CON-SUP-110 reset deadline from an instant when the signals are low, which can describe a whole interval. OP-SYS-033 acknowledges the missing alignment in addition to the separate decision about a later fault.
findings.requested_change: Use the defined safe-state entry event for the first fault's reset deadline and keep any change to that deadline for a later fault subject to the precedence decision in OP-SYS-033.

findings.description: SYS-WDG-006 expires the window after 12 ms without a further refresh. CON-SUP-106 makes a refresh later than 12 ms invalid, and SYS-TEST-012 accepts spacing of exactly 12 ms. The set gives no ordering for a refresh coincident with expiry, so the watchdog and demonstration can yield different outcomes at that boundary.
findings.requested_change: Define the refresh-versus-expiry ordering at exactly 12 ms consistently with CON-SUP-106, and use it in the watchdog and demonstration verdicts.

findings.description: The trace matrix gives derivation links for SYS-TEST-005 from CON-SUP-108 and for SYS-TEST-010 and SYS-TEST-012 from the cycle and watchdog constraints. These items are marked derived=false even though their rationales say the timing origin or counts rely on unapproved assumptions. The links identify the related inputs but misstate the basis for the normative test targets.
findings.requested_change: Identify direct obligations and proposed derivations accurately in the items and trace. Trace the demonstration targets to approved premises or retain them as open proposals pending a decision.

findings.description: A refresh follows the completed flow check under SYS-WDG-003. With 10 ms cycle boundaries and variable delays from those boundaries to refresh, the inter-refresh interval is 10 ms plus the change in delay between cycles. CON-SUP-106 limits that interval to 6–12 ms. OP-SYS-013 identifies execution loads, but the set gives no bound or feasibility criterion for that variation.
findings.requested_change: Assess the variation in cycle-end-to-refresh delay under the configured schedule, including flow checking and interference, and link its allowable range to the window-watchdog limits.

findings.description: SYS-RST-004 through SYS-RST-007 and SYS-DIAG-010 depend on state that survives software and watchdog resets under CON-SUP-110. The environment analysis leaves open whether the selected target and Renode model preserve the relevant state through those reset paths and whether a reset during an update leaves a usable record. OP-SYS-015 and OP-SYS-022 address required history contents, but do not establish these platform capabilities.
findings.requested_change: Record the platform and simulator dependencies for retaining reset-sequence state, the latch and history, including interrupted updates. Assign an evidence method for each retention property.

findings.description: SYS-BL-1 is marked draft, but several open points that change required outcomes are marked blocks=false. For example, OP-SYS-027 changes which releases satisfy CON-SUP-103, OP-SYS-007 changes the timing verdict under CON-SUP-112 and CON-SUP-113, and OP-SYS-015 changes the reset-surviving history. The disposition understates what needs agreement before those outcomes can be baselined.
findings.requested_change: Reconcile open-point blocking flags and affected-item statuses with the unresolved changes to behavior and verification, and identify the decisions or evidence required to close them.

findings.description: Suppressing T_IN completion can also suppress its checkpoint or force a timing fault, depending on the hook behavior and checkpoint source. Under SYS-SUP-005 and SYS-WDG-007, an earlier flow or timing fault can initiate reset before the two-period alive window expires. SYS-TEST-015 gives no validity criterion that distinguishes a masked alive test from a failure of alive supervision.
findings.requested_change: Show that the stimulus prevents completion without an earlier competing fault, or define another observation that isolates the alive monitor. Treat runs masked by an earlier fault or reset as invalid for the positive control.

findings.description: The refresh interval applies whenever no listed task fault has been detected since reset. This includes startup and a retained safe-state latch, where CON-SUP-106 does not establish when independent-watchdog servicing applies and OP-SYS-010 remains open.
findings.requested_change: Specify the operating states in which the independent watchdog is serviced and the event that anchors its first refresh interval.

findings.description: Stopping both refreshes on a task fault can put the CON-SUP-106 window-watchdog reset ahead of the report and software reset in CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112. The required outcome near window expiry remains unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Align refresh cessation with the approved precedence for hardware expiry, reporting and software reset.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-110 latch rule still leaves the effect of an intervening watchdog or other reset undefined. The rationale describes fault-free operation after successful startup, but the normative text does not identify the event that starts the 60 s interval.
findings.requested_change: State which intervening events break the sequence and identify the approved start event for counting 60 s of fault-free operation.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires a startup message carrying the reset cause. Without the framing and encoding left open in OP-SYS-002, the verifier cannot identify the message and decode a cause.
findings.requested_change: Reference an approved startup-message format and give the expected encoding for each reset class.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the service tool to read the reset cause. Neither response in CON-SUP-113 includes it and other requests receive ERR. The set leaves the interaction that satisfies both constraints open.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved service interaction that delivers the cause, and reconcile it with the CON-SUP-113 response rules.

findings.description: The 10 ms requirement leaves it open whether to time the first transmitted bit or completion of the terminating line feed. The rationale selects completion while OP-SYS-007 records that the CON-SUP-112 endpoint is undecided.
findings.requested_change: State the approved observable endpoint for the 10 ms deadline in the requirement and use it in verification.

findings.description: The report is due for every detected fault under CON-SUP-112. SYS-WDG-005 can cause a CON-SUP-106 reset before transmission starts or completes. The report obligation in that case remains undefined.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved watchdog precedence to define the required report outcome when reset preempts transmission.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-003 assigns code 8 to a watchdog reset and SYS-DIAG-002 requires an entity. The task names, CODE and CONFIG in CON-SUP-112 leave code 8 without an entity value.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved entity value for a watchdog-reset report.

findings.description: The affected task is ambiguous when several checkpoints are missing or out of order in one CON-SUP-104 evaluation. The set leaves the entity required by CON-SUP-112 undecided in that case.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved task-selection and reporting rule for flow faults involving one or multiple incorrect checkpoints.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 gives milliseconds since start without defining the reference event. The item selects the latest reset and uses 'the controller started', which identifies no observable event while OP-SYS-007 remains unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved timestamp origin as an observable event and apply it after each relevant reset class.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 supplies the STS template, but the request boundary, legal state values and meaning of fault count remain open. A verifier cannot form a complete request and predict the response for a known state and history.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved request framing, state encoding and fault-count semantics.

findings.description: The 50 ms deadline from CON-SUP-113 leaves request receipt and response transmission without agreed measurement endpoints. A reply that starts within 50 ms and finishes later has no unique verdict.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable request and response events that bound the GET STATUS response time.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 requires the last eight reports, but the set leaves their wire order and response framing open. A verifier cannot distinguish a complete response holding fewer than eight reports, including an empty response, from an incomplete transmission.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved record order, framing and completion indication for histories containing zero through eight reports.

findings.description: The 50 ms deadline from CON-SUP-113 has no agreed request-side event or endpoint for a multi-record response. A reply may start within 50 ms and finish after it.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable request and response events that bound the GET FAULTS response time.

findings.description: The GET FAULTS trigger has no mode qualification. A CON-SUP-110 reset can interrupt an accepted response, and the set leaves acceptance and response behavior in the latched safe state open.
findings.requested_change: Define acceptance during pending reset and latched operation, and state the expected outcome when reset overtakes an accepted request.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 requires ERR for other requests. Without request framing or an approved response bound, a test cannot establish when recognition is due or distinguish a missing ERR from a delayed one.
findings.requested_change: Define how an unrecognized request is delimited and give the approved deadline for observing its ERR response.

findings.description: CON-SUP-114 requires processor-use measurement at the configured core clock. The set gives neither the clock setting nor a controlled simulator configuration that supplies it, so the result is not reproducible.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved clock setting or controlled simulator configuration for the processor-use test.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires rejection of unknown tasks. CON-SUP-101 gives the configured tasks but leaves the supported identifier set open. The expected verdict for an identifier outside the default configuration is therefore undefined.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved supported-task set and use it to select known and unknown identifiers for verification.

findings.description: STK-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-107 identify the application image and when to check it. The approved integrity criterion and reference needed for an independent accept-or-reject verdict remain open.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved integrity criterion and reference information used to establish the expected result for each test image.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 gives the CRC-32 polynomial. Different initialization, reflection and final XOR settings can produce different check values for the same block while using that polynomial.
findings.requested_change: Reference the complete approved CRC-32 parameters so an independent verifier can compute the expected value.

findings.description: A flow fault at the end of a nominal 10 ms cycle can suppress the refresh with about 2 ms remaining before the CON-SUP-106 timeout. That reset can preempt the CON-SUP-110 software reset request and prevent it from counting toward the latch.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved reset precedence and state the required reset outcome and timing when hardware expiry competes with the software reset request.

findings.description: The software reset is required after a failed startup computation. With a watchdog active during the check, the remaining time after failure may be insufficient for the CON-SUP-110 report and reset sequence. Startup watchdog operation and the available time remain open.
findings.requested_change: Resolve startup watchdog operation and establish the time available for reporting and requesting reset after a failed computation.

findings.description: The terminating line feed must precede a software reset request. If refreshes stop and CON-SUP-106 resets the controller first, that ordering can hold vacuously while the CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112 report is interrupted.
findings.requested_change: State the required transmission outcome when the hardware reset preempts the intended software reset request.

findings.description: The test must establish both outputs low from any reset under CON-SUP-109. CON-SUP-003 and CON-SUP-005 do not establish that the simulator represents external pin levels during reset assertion and before software configures the pins.
findings.requested_change: Use a verification method that establishes both output levels through reset and software takeover for every applicable reset path.

findings.description: CON-SUP-109 requires status low from any reset, including one taken while SYS-SAFE-006 has status high. The stated test lacks evidence that the external status level is represented while reset is asserted and before software acts.
findings.requested_change: Establish how the external status level will be verified from reset assertion through software takeover for each applicable reset path.

findings.description: The startup fault test samples the two outputs from the preceding reset. A trace beginning once the test build runs cannot establish the continuous low interval required by CON-SUP-109 through reset assertion and early startup.
findings.requested_change: Combine the injected-fault test with verification evidence covering both outputs from reset assertion to the earliest supported test observation.

findings.description: The fault test can observe status low at injection and still miss a high level during the preceding reset. CON-SUP-109 and this item require the full, uninterrupted low interval.
findings.requested_change: Cover reset assertion and the pre-software interval as well as the startup fault interval in the status verification.

findings.description: The item excludes a period whose control cycle starts before checks pass. CON-SUP-107 bars early task release but does not rule out a scheduled release later in that same cycle. CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-102 leave that alignment and the first T_DIAG release phase open.
findings.requested_change: Define the first counted window and latest alive detection point for each task using the approved startup and release alignment.

findings.description: A preempted task can use less processor time than its CON-SUP-103 limit while exceeding the same limit in elapsed time. The no-overrun outcome depends on the measurement basis left open in OP-SYS-013.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved execution-time basis for the no-overrun rule and include a preempted execution in the boundary checks.

findings.description: The 12 ms expiry is referenced to a previous refresh, leaving no expiry reference if the window watchdog becomes active and its first refresh never occurs. That case matters to the fallback reset in STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Define the activation event and the interval that governs expiry before the first accepted refresh.

findings.description: This item requires all detected faults in history, while SYS-DIAG-010 allows entry as late as the first transmitted bit. A query or reset between detection and entry yields different history outcomes. CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113 leave that interval open.
findings.requested_change: Set a single history membership event and define the expected query and retained contents before entry and after an intervening reset.

findings.description: The proposed test sets reset flags and checks that classification follows the flags. CON-SUP-111 names five classes but gives no expected mapping or precedence for combined flags or flags retained from an earlier reset.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved classification rule and give expected classes for single, combined and retained flag patterns.

findings.description: The text requires detection at the exact execution-limit expiry. The rationale says exact declaration is infeasible and proposes an unapproved tolerance. The measurement resolution in CON-SUP-103 does not supply that tolerance.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the permitted latency from expiry and apply the same declaration bound in the requirement and verification.

findings.description: This item declares an overrun when execution is incomplete at expiry, while SYS-SUP-007 forbids one for a completion measured at or below the limit. With a mapping left open by OP-SYS-027, a completion just after expiry can meet both conditions.
findings.requested_change: Use a consistent basis for expiry and the no-overrun decision, and verify completion at expiry and just after it when the observation maps to the limit.

findings.description: With truncation and a 2 ms limit, a start at 2.05 ms can be measured at 2.0 ms and be accepted by this item. CON-SUP-103 classifies a start later than the limit as late. OP-SYS-027 has not resolved how the measurement maps times near the limit.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the mapping of actual start times to the measured boundary and verify a start immediately beyond the limit against the approved interpretation.

findings.description: This demonstration checks for the presence of the CON-SUP-111 startup message. Without a defined message identity, the procedure cannot distinguish that message from startup FLT or other simulated serial output.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved startup-message identity to define what the simulated serial capture must contain.

findings.description: When equally timed faults straddle the eight-report cutoff, either report can be displaced under the current wording. CON-SUP-113 gives the count but leaves the tie unresolved, changing the GET FAULTS result.
findings.requested_change: Specify how equally timed reports are ordered at the cutoff and verify which report is retained.

findings.description: From the eighth detection onward this item changes required history membership at detection, while SYS-DIAG-010 allows later entry. A query or reset before entry leaves both the new and the displaced report unresolved under CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved history membership event to define the retained set on each side of that event and after an intervening reset.

findings.description: The ordering applies only if the startup failure leads to a software reset request. A watchdog active during startup can reset after the failing computation and before either reporting or the request. CON-SUP-106 and CON-SUP-107 give no timing basis that excludes this case.
findings.requested_change: Resolve startup watchdog operation and define how the report sequence is preserved or handled if expiry intervenes.

findings.description: The continuous CON-SUP-109 and CON-SUP-110 hold includes reset assertion and the interval before software acts. CON-SUP-003 gives no pin or board evidence that both outputs remain driven low, and sampled simulator values cannot establish the whole interval.
findings.requested_change: Establish the pin and board behavior for the reset paths and plan verification that covers the complete low-output interval.

findings.description: The latched status hold spans each reset, but CON-SUP-003 gives no external pin behavior during reset or before software configures it. A simulator result showing no high sample does not establish continuous low status over that interval.
findings.requested_change: Establish how the external status level is held low through the reset paths and verify the complete hold interval.

findings.description: The only history-entry deadline is the first transmitted bit. A watchdog reset that prevents transmission from starting leaves no expected history outcome. CON-SUP-110 requires survival of the history across that reset, and OP-SYS-015 leaves entry of the detected fault open.
findings.requested_change: Specify whether the report must appear when reset prevents transmission from starting and verify that case.

findings.description: The first-bit reset test reads GET FAULTS only after restart. Startup can reconstruct the report from separately retained data even when the history entry was incomplete at the first bit. The test cannot distinguish retention under CON-SUP-110 from the required entry order.
findings.requested_change: Observe durable history-entry completion and the first transmitted bit on a common time base. Verify the post-reset outcome separately.

findings.description: The valid-start test treats absence of a first release as failure. CON-SUP-107 and this item impose a release gate and give no deadline for a release. A run with no release cannot exercise the ordering comparison.
findings.requested_change: Classify a run without a release as inconclusive for the ordering check, or judge missing release against a separately sourced startup progression requirement.

findings.description: The timing test equates full-pass completion with processing the segment ending at __app_end without a fault. A pass that skips an earlier segment can satisfy that criterion while violating the full-image obligation in CON-SUP-108 and SYS-MEM-007.
findings.requested_change: Count completion only when the pass trace shows full image coverage, and apply the 11 s bounds to those verified completion events.

findings.description: The supplementary test requires code 7 on the line in the cycle that processed the corrupt segment. CON-SUP-105 anchors detection to completion of the failing computation, OP-SYS-005 leaves the integrity method open, and CON-SUP-112 allows serial transmission within 10 ms of detection.
findings.requested_change: Verify segment cadence using the range trace, and judge diagnostic timing from the failing computation applicable to the selected integrity method.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 orders safe-state entry before report transmission. SYS-WDG-007 can withhold a refresh and trigger the CON-SUP-106 reset before either event. The item has no outcome for this preemption.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved watchdog precedence and give a verdict for a reset before safe-state entry or the start of transmission.

findings.description: The text prohibits output rises 'between' the CON-SUP-105 event and the next reset. The rationale rejects a rise at the event itself. These readings give different verdicts for a coincident low-to-high transition.
findings.requested_change: State explicitly whether the prohibition includes the fault event and where it ends at reset, using the same endpoints in verification.

findings.description: The text prohibits a status rise 'between' the CON-SUP-105 event and the next reset, while the rationale rejects a rise at the event itself. A coincident transition has different verdicts under the text and test.
findings.requested_change: State the inclusion rule for the fault event and the reset boundary explicitly in the requirement and test.

findings.description: The proposed comparison uses the first measured value above the limit as the reference for a future detection deadline. OP-SYS-025 asks for a decision from configured limit expiry. CON-SUP-103 quantization can separate those events and cause the test to accept an overdue declaration.
findings.requested_change: Record limit expiry and measured crossing separately, and trace the comparison to the approved origin for any separate declaration deadline.

findings.description: The sweep accepts multiples of 100 µs if two values are 100 µs apart. An output alternating between 0 and 100 µs regardless of injected delay passes, although CON-SUP-103 requires measuring the delay from release to start.
findings.requested_change: Verify that the readout tracks the injected release-to-start interval as well as its increment, and apply the approved mapping when it is available.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 and CON-SUP-105 put the flow check and fault event at cycle end. OP-SYS-036 leaves receipt at the same instant undecided, so the same trace can yield an arrived checkpoint or a flow fault.
findings.requested_change: Resolve receipt-versus-evaluation precedence at the boundary and apply it to the coincident-receipt test.

findings.description: The multiple-of-100 µs and one-pair criteria can pass values unrelated to execution time or measured from the wrong start event. They do not verify the start-to-completion or start-to-expiry intervals required by this item and grounded in CON-SUP-103.
findings.requested_change: Compare the readout with independently observed execution intervals in completion and overrun runs, applying the approved time basis and quantization.

findings.description: Analysis criterion (d) forbids carrying prior-cycle count or order state into evaluation. CON-SUP-104 limits what can affect the result. Retained cycle-tagged state can be ignored before it influences evaluation and still fail criterion (d).
findings.requested_change: Require evidence that every retained state path leaves current-cycle presence, count and order unaffected by prior-cycle checkpoints.

findings.description: The nominal run observes a status edge and the three failure runs observe status held low. All four can pass if the valid path drives status high before the checks finish and the injected-failure paths suppress the edge. That evidence does not establish the CON-SUP-109 ordering.
findings.requested_change: Observe successful completion of every startup check and the status edge on a common time base in the nominal run, and compare their order.

findings.description: The item mandates 11 s of continuous high status from the status edge. CON-SUP-108 gives 11 s for a full runtime integrity pass with a different origin. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 give no high-status demonstration duration.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved demonstration duration and timing origin in this item and its dependent cases.

findings.description: An absent FLT prefix does not establish absence of declarations. A late fault can leave a partial prefix after the high-status observation ends, or the capture can close before the prefix completes under a start-of-transmission interpretation of CON-SUP-112. A subsequent service reply and an alive positive-control run can still pass.
findings.requested_change: Use capture and frame criteria that cover the approved report deadline and account for truncation. Observe declarations directly where the verdict claims their absence.

findings.description: The observation ends at a complete code 5 report, but the run does not establish an otherwise valid startup or define the verdict if the report never arrives. A configuration fault can hold status low and mask the CON-SUP-107 code-integrity case.
findings.requested_change: Isolate the code-integrity failure in an otherwise valid setup and define a finite observation with a complete code 5 report required to pass.

findings.description: The run does not establish an intact code image or define a verdict if no code 6 report arrives. A code-integrity failure can keep status low without exercising the configuration-integrity check in CON-SUP-107.
findings.requested_change: Use an intact application image, isolate the configuration-integrity failure and require a complete code 6 report within a defined observation interval.

findings.description: The run does not establish that both integrity checks can pass with the range-fault stimulus. A change invalidating the stored CRC can produce code 6, keeping status low without exercising CON-SUP-115. There is no finite observation criterion when code 9 is absent.
findings.requested_change: Define a range-fault stimulus that preserves application and configuration integrity, and require a complete code 9 report within a defined observation interval.

findings.description: The threshold of 1099 complete cycles assumes the first cycle begins within 10 ms of the status edge. CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-109 specify the cycle and the signal without bounding the interval between these events.
findings.requested_change: Derive the count from approved first-cycle alignment and observation duration, or anchor observation to a recorded cycle boundary.

findings.description: Completion is due by the execution-limit expiry of each scheduled release. A task that is never released or never starts has no execution-limit expiry under SYS-SUP-003. The criterion leaves that missing CON-SUP-101 slot without a finite failure verdict.
findings.requested_change: Enumerate the expected release slots independently of observed releases and define finite failure criteria for missing release or start before checking completion deadlines.

findings.description: The threshold of 1098 refreshes inherits the unapproved first-cycle delay in SYS-TEST-010. CON-SUP-106 gives cycle-end and inter-refresh rules but no count measured from the status edge.
findings.requested_change: Use the approved cycle and observation alignment to derive a count, or judge refreshes against the observed eligible cycle ends.

findings.description: The count and 6–12 ms spacing can pass for refreshes displaced from cycle ends or with a missed refresh at one cycle end and an extra refresh elsewhere. The test does not establish the once-per-cycle end-of-cycle service in CON-SUP-106.
findings.requested_change: Associate refreshes with eligible cycle ends and check both the required service per cycle and the observed inter-refresh intervals.

findings.description: The interval that 'contains no refresh' has ambiguous endpoints. With inclusive endpoints, refreshes exactly 100 ms apart can satisfy the text even though SYS-WDG-004 requires a gap shorter than the CON-SUP-106 timeout.
findings.requested_change: Define the leading, trailing and inter-refresh interval boundaries and give an explicit verdict for a gap of exactly 100 ms.

findings.description: The demonstration mandates a line feed though CON-SUP-113 does not specify one for STS. CON-SUP-112 specifies it for FLT. The demonstration also accepts a bare STS prefix and line feed without the two fields required by CON-SUP-113.
findings.requested_change: Verify that the response contains both fields and remove the unsupported terminator from the pass criteria pending approved response framing.

findings.description: The item selects the end of the request as the time origin and leaves the response endpoint open. OP-SYS-007 records the CON-SUP-113 timing references as undecided. A response that begins before the deadline and ends after it has no unique verdict.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved request and response timing reference events to the demonstration.

findings.description: The 40 ms derivation assumes T_IN periods are already progressing at injection. An offset of 100 ms from the status edge does not establish that condition under CON-SUP-101 or CON-SUP-102. OP-SYS-020 leaves first-cycle alignment open, so the test can reject a controller that satisfies the alive rule.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the injection against observed T_IN period boundaries in a separate positive-control run and derive its deadline from the resulting alive-window expiry and approved report endpoint.

findings.description: The refresh cutoff uses physical start-limit expiry while SYS-SUP-002 declares lateness from the first measured value above the limit. If a refresh falls between those events, the duty to refresh can depend on whether the task later starts before the measured crossing.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the late-start mapping and define a cutoff that can be evaluated at the refresh instant. Use the same cutoff in SYS-WDG-007.

findings.description: Fault-free run V1 accepts a refresh anywhere between successive cycle boundaries after the flow check. It can pass alternating early and late refreshes outside the CON-SUP-106 window and does not establish end-of-cycle service.
findings.requested_change: Verify the relationship between cycle end, flow-check completion and refresh, and check spacing against the 6–12 ms window.

findings.description: The inclusive prohibition can yield a CON-SUP-106 watchdog reset 12 ms after the previous refresh. This can interrupt the CON-SUP-110 report-then-software-reset sequence and does not count as a supervisor reset for the latch.
findings.requested_change: Apply the approved precedence for watchdog reset, reporting and software reset, including the effect on the latch sequence.

findings.description: The prohibition includes refresh coincident with cutoff. V3 places expiry strictly before or after the reference refresh, and neither the additional overrun run nor the cycle-boundary runs establish that a refresh would otherwise fall exactly at cutoff. An implementation that prohibits refresh only strictly after cutoff can pass.
findings.requested_change: Add a valid case or analysis that distinguishes a refresh at cutoff from one immediately before it.
